title: Lissity propagates through powers of an ideal
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], $B$ a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], and $J\subset B$ an ideal. Use constant coefficient sheaves [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and derived scalar extension [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. Let $K\in D^-(\mathcal C,\underline B)$, meaning its cohomology vanishes in sufficiently high degrees. Suppose every cohomology sheaf of $K\otimes_B^L B/J$ is locally isomorphic to the constant sheaf associated to a finitely generated $B/J$-module. Then every cohomology sheaf of $K\otimes_B^L B/J^m$ is locally isomorphic to the constant sheaf associated to a finitely generated $B/J^m$-module for every $m\geq1$. If $J^m=0$, this conclusion applies to $K$ itself.

proof.text: Let $\mathscr L_B$ be the full subcategory of sheaves of $\underline B$-modules locally isomorphic to constant sheaves of finitely generated $B$-modules. It contains zero and is invariant under isomorphism. By [lem-weil-pbc-locally-constant-derived-serre] it is closed under kernels, cokernels, and extensions. Apply [lem-sbc-cohomology-in-weak-serre-subcategory] to the abelian category [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]: complexes with cohomology in $\mathscr L_B$ form a full triangulated subcategory. Thus the two outer terms of a distinguished triangle belonging to it imply that the middle term belongs to it.

source.place: Tag 094I, proof, paragraph beginning 'Recall that the locally constant sheaves'

proof.text: Put $Q_n=J^n/J^{n+1}$. The quotient sequence $0\to Q_n\to B/J^{n+1}\to B/J^n\to0$ is exact. Constant presheaves preserve it objectwise, and [lem-weil-pbc-site-module-presheaf-sheafification-exact] makes its constant-sheaf sequence exact. Choose a K-flat resolution $P\to K$ with flat terms using [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. Flatness [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules] makes $0\to P\otimes_B\underline{Q_n}\to P\otimes_B\underline{B/J^{n+1}}\to P\otimes_B\underline{B/J^n}\to0$ degreewise exact. Its cone identifies the usual short-exact-complex triangle (the kernel of the cone-to-quotient map is the contractible cone of the identity). Thus it gives the triangle in Tag 094I. For the scalar identification, $P\otimes_B\underline{B/J}$ is K-flat over $\underline{B/J}$: tensoring it with an acyclic quotient-module complex gives $P\otimes_B N$, acyclic by K-flatness [def-pc-kflat-complex]. Ordinary balancing then gives $(P\otimes_B\underline{B/J})\otimes_{B/J}\underline{Q_n}\cong P\otimes_B\underline{Q_n}$, sending $(p\otimes\bar b)\otimes q$ to $p\otimes bq$, with inverse $p\otimes q\mapsto(p\otimes1)\otimes q$. These maps commute with differentials and restrictions, so compute the asserted derived identification by [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings].

source.place: Tag 094I, proof, displayed distinguished triangles and isomorphisms

proof.text: The base case $n=1$ is the hypothesis. The quotient $B/J$ is Noetherian: lift an ideal to $B$ and project its finitely many generators. Also $J^n$ is a finitely generated ideal by [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]; its generators project to generators of $Q_n$ over $B/J$, because $JQ_n=0$. Consequently $\underline{Q_n}[0]$ is locally constant of finite type over $B/J$. The reduction $K\otimes_B^L\underline{B/J}$ is bounded above: first replace any representative by its good truncation at the upper bound $b$: replace the term in degree $b$ by the kernel of its outgoing differential and set all higher terms to zero. Since cohomology above $b$ is zero, the inclusion is a quasi-isomorphism. Apply [lem-pc-kflat-bounded-flat-replacement] and [lem-pc-bounded-above-flat-kflat-site] to obtain a K-flat flat representative with no terms above $b$; its tensor with a degree-zero coefficient module has no terms above $b$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-locally-constant-tensor] over $B/J$ to obtain locally constant finite-type cohomology for the first triangle term of Step 2. Restricting these sheaves to $B$ preserves local constant finite-module descriptions. If the last triangle term has that property by induction, the triangulated closure from Step 1 [lem-sbc-cohomology-in-weak-serre-subcategory] implies it for the middle term. To recover its $B/J^{n+1}$-module local descriptions, choose finite generators $j_1,\ldots,j_t$ of $J^{n+1}$. On any constant $B$-module trivialization $\underline M$ the actions of these generators vanish as sheaf morphisms. Their module images therefore have zero constant sheaf; replace $M$ by $M/J^{n+1}M$, which has the same constant sheaf by exact sheafification [lem-weil-pbc-site-module-presheaf-sheafification-exact]. This quotient is a finite $B/J^{n+1}$-module and the isomorphism is quotient-linear. The induction proves every required reduction.

source.place: Tag 094I, proof, final paragraph ('Combined with Lemma ... we obtain the result')

proof.text: If $J^m=0$, then $B/J^m=B$ and the canonical derived scalar-extension map identifies $K\otimes_B^L\underline{B/J^m}$ with $K$; hence the preceding conclusion applies directly to every cohomology sheaf of $K$. On a K-flat model $P$, this is the chain isomorphism $P\otimes_B\underline B\to P$, $p\otimes b\mapsto bp$, with inverse $p\mapsto p\otimes1$.
